summary: All platforms under 100 followers. Instagram reels lose 77% viewers in first 3 seconds; last 4 posts zero engagement. Bio violates brand rules: niches, region, timeframe, free offer. Chatbot posts show relative strength (1.27x) but data is thin.
guidance:
- Hook: try **contrast** (1.75x, n=1) or **question** (1.7x, n=2) — rotate away from top3 (overused, 5 posts).
- Avoid: "Top 3 reasons…" phrasing (repeated 3× in 7 days), lead-gen comparison posts (0 engagement), animated ads (0.57x).
- Post must read like a developer sharing real work, not an ad. No demos, samples, or niche targeting.
- First 3 seconds must stop scroll: open with a relatable pain point (e.g., "Customer asks at 11 PM, you reply at 9 AM") not a list.

instructions.research: Find 2-3 common late-night/weekend customer questions across varied Indian small businesses (clinic, gym, D2C, coaching) — no niche focus.
instructions.analysis: Compare the 3 published chatbot posts (question, top3, top3) — note which phrasing got 13 engagements vs zeros; extract the winning hook pattern.
instructions.writer: Write one Instagram carousel/text post: hook = contrast (day vs night reply gap), body = how a chatbot handles repeated questions 24/7, close = "Pay after approval. DM for honest advice if this fits." No demo, no niche, no timeframe.
instructions.image: Create a simple chat-card graphic showing an example conversation (labelled "Example") — user asks at 23:12, bot replies instantly. Clean, code-like aesthetic. No logos, no client names.
instructions.video: Skip video today; reel hook failure rate is 77%. Focus on static carousel for higher retention.

manual_tips: Update Instagram bio to: "Websites, AI chatbots & lead gen for small businesses across India. Pay after approval. DM for honest advice." (removes niche, region, timeframe, free offer)
Comment thoughtfully on 5 posts from Indian small business owners (clinics, gyms, D2C brands) — ask about their after-hours enquiries, don't pitch.
Reply to any story mentions or tags from the last week; keep it conversational, not promotional.
